implementerProof.how: Drove every surface again with Dispatch built by the tester from the workspace (head) and from git archive c3d09eec (base) on INFRA-589's load-test stack. Proofs 1 (bounded catch-up), 2 (relay and hub reads), 4 (agent-stream byte budget), 5 (restart before and after: 1.48 MB against 122.0 MB replayed, 60 against 300 refetch requests) and 6 (docs) reproduce. Proof 3 does not prove its criterion: at its 500 ms listener round trip every lookup is cut at mentionLookupTimeout (250 ms), so its 0.653 s comment is the mention lookups' timeout plus the issue route's lookup timeout in series, not 'about one 500 ms round trip'; lat.sh shows the same 0.61-0.72 s against a listener that never answers, which is the failure below.

failures.criterion: Mention delivery runs off the request path, in order, with a test that a slow listener does not delay the comment's response (architect's amendment, dispatch://INFRA-606/comment/cf41ba1a-6223-4121-87f7-9fd8239479b3: the lookup gets a timeout of at most 250 ms, and a listener that never answers delays comment creation by at most the timeout).
failures.evidence: With Dispatch's ENVOY_URL through 'loadgen proxy -rtt 30s' (a listener that never answers), lat.sh posts 5 comments per shape at head 153513a3: no mention 0.091-0.101 s; one mention on an issue with no route 0.361-0.392 s; one mention that is the issue's route 0.356-0.370 s; one mention on an issue routed to another session 0.612-0.644 s; three mentions on such an issue 0.631-0.718 s. The routed case pays two 250 ms timeouts in series: resolveMentionTargets runs first (comment_create.go:376), then resolveCommentRoute looks the route up with its own mentionLookupTimeout (comment_create.go:289) inside resolveThenLock. Every seeded issue carries a route, as Legion's issues do. The existing test bound (commentWithAnUnansweredLookup: mentionLookupTimeout + 500 ms) holds only one lookup path, so it cannot see this. Red test: TestAListenerThatAnswersNoLookupDelaysARoutedCommentByOneTimeoutAtMost in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/comment_delivery_sender_test.go (commit 'test(dispatch): a silent listener delays a routed mentioned comment by one lookup timeout at most'); `cd packages/envoy && GOWORK=off DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<postgres url> go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run TestAListenerThatAnswersNoLookupDelaysARoutedCommentByOneTimeoutAtMost -count=1` fails: 'the comment answered after 530.805161ms with no lookup answered, want under 500ms'. The same file's single-timeout cases answer in 276 ms, so a route lookup run beside the mention lookups passes it.

observations: Criterion 5 is measured on the restart-scenario patch, not on a committed harness: INFRA-589's PR #2369 is still open, and the architect scheduled the harness commit and five runs per side for the round after it merges (dispatch://INFRA-606/comment/b7beb47e-3229-477c-9f93-e00c586c0cfb).

A process killed during its mention sends (mention.sh kill9) leaves the attempts in flight pending with a claim younger than one minute; the next process's recovery pass skips them and runs only at start, so those recipients get the later comments and never that one, until the author retries or a later start finds the claim lapsed. The plan dropped the claim-lapse re-check on purpose (Decision 8); base strands the same attempts and more.

The Stage 3 production audit now reads only events of issues updated since the baseline (as stage4b's does) plus the projects list. audit.sh shows it misses a rig-authored event that belongs to no issue: a project document a rig session uploads to another project (artifact.created, issue_key null) passes it, where the old full-stream replay would have failed it. Sent to the architect for a decision.
